Tech Scan: AI gateway

When several agents call models or tools, a gateway can give the team a shared place to route requests and apply controls. Choose the missing capability first: model routing, tool access and usage reporting are related, but they are not interchangeable.

Draft research reference. Based on published documentation, not local deployment tests.

For the surrounding concepts, read Equip the agent and Supply relevant information.

On this page
Separate model routing from tool access AWS-first default Controls and common mistakes Gaps and open questions Sources

For model selection and access routes, see Tech Scan: Models.

Separate model routing from tool access

A gateway centralises controls for requests that pass through it, such as provider credentials, routing and usage limits. IAM and client configuration can also restrict model access without a gateway; the benefit is a shared enforcement point, not the creation of model policy.

Separate the two responsibilities before choosing a product. One product may support both:

  • A large language model (LLM) router sends model calls to configured providers and models. Depending on the product, it can also manage credentials, fallback and usage limits.
  • A tool/MCP gateway routes tool calls. It exposes approved tools — including MCP servers and knowledge bases — to the agent under policy, and records which tools were called.

The Harness reference covers the agent loop that makes these calls. For the AWS-first route, distinguish the traffic it sends:

  • Model calls reach approved models through Bedrock, directly or through a configured inference proxy.
  • Tool calls can reach approved tools and MCP servers through AgentCore Gateway.
  • Retrieval can use a Managed Knowledge Base exposed as a Gateway target.

AWS-first default

Keep approved Claude and OpenAI access through Bedrock as the baseline.[4][5] Add a gateway where shared routing or control is needed, rather than treating every model call as a reason to build a larger stack.

AgentCore Gateway inference targets provide a unified LLM proxy for Amazon Bedrock, OpenAI and Anthropic, alongside other OpenAI-compatible services.[17] These model targets are distinct from the Gateway's MCP and tool targets. Provider support does not approve a direct-provider route or establish feature parity.

Gateway rules configure model routing and fallback for inference targets.[18] Every fallback destination still needs approval. Check the selected region, model, operation and API dialect before relying on the route; one supported endpoint does not establish support for every API.

Add only the controls the use case needs. The components have different responsibilities:

AWS-first gateway components
ComponentWhat it doesWhat it does not do
Amazon BedrockModel API for approved Claude and OpenAI modelsProvide every gateway control by itself
AgentCore Gateway inference targetsProxy model calls; rules can route and fall back across targetsApprove a provider or model on the team's behalf
AgentCore Gateway tool/MCP targetsExpose configured tools to the agentControl traffic that bypasses the Gateway
Bedrock GuardrailsContent guardrails on model callsAuthorise tool calls
AgentCore Policy (Cedar)Authorises configured Gateway requestsGovern arbitrary shell networking

Gateway policy governs traffic through the Gateway, not arbitrary shell networking.[3] VPC attachment alone is not evidence of package-only egress or secret denial: outbound enforcement, approved dependencies and credential protection still need their own controls.

A Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base can be exposed through AgentCore Gateway.[6] Begin with Retrieve plus an approved Claude or OpenAI model for generation,[7] with embeddings and reranking approved separately.[9]

ACL-aware retrieval respects access control lists, but the managed service does not authenticate the end user: the application supplies verified identity.[8] A shared retrieval endpoint cannot replace that identity check.

Match other controls to their enforcement points

The AgentCore harness can use these managed components,[1] but each control needs its own scope. IAM sets identity and resource boundaries; AgentCore Policy uses Cedar for configured Gateway authorisation.[2]

CloudFormation Guard checks structured data.[10] It is not interchangeable with request authorisation or content guardrails. None of these components implies complete policy-framework coverage or replaces retained human decisions.

Conditional alternatives

First name the capability the Bedrock and AgentCore baseline cannot meet. Then consider existing infrastructure and who will operate the alternative. Being on AWS, Kubernetes or a managed service does not by itself decide the gateway.

Consider LiteLLM proxy when the required routing behaviour is missing from the baseline and the team can operate another service. LiteLLM documents load balancing, fallbacks, timeouts and retries across deployments and providers.[20] Compare the exact configuration and operating cost, not just the provider count.

Any alternative still needs the required API, approved data location and retention, identity, security boundaries and an operational owner. A hosted gateway's supported-model catalogue is not the team's approved list; restrict every primary and fallback route accordingly.

The earlier secondary comparison retains useful research leads, but its packaging, licensing and product-history claims are not independently verified in this refinement.[12] Licensing, incident and lifecycle claims need current first-party terms, advisories or announcements before they inform adoption.

Research-only notes

Langfuse now documents a separate AI Gateway in public beta. It proxies OpenAI and Anthropic requests, centralises provider keys, records usage and supports central model approval.[19] This is a different capability from its existing observability deployment on AWS.[13]

Provider fallbacks, hard spend caps and automatic task-based model routing are roadmap items, not implemented features.[19] Keep this option research-only until its available features meet the requirement and the provider route passes the same data, identity and model-policy checks as any other alternative. Langfuse observability on AWS does not establish a Bedrock route through this beta gateway.

Controls and common mistakes

Direct provider APIs remain exceptions for a specific capability or approved-region gap, after reviewing egress, credentials, retention and data handling. A gateway's provider support does not grant that exception.

  • Do not present any gateway as a substitute for the model policy. The policy is managed Claude or OpenAI models only; a gateway does not change which models are approved.
  • Keep primary calls, fallback, managed defaults, retrieval reasoning and evaluator models inside the approved list. Automatic routing cannot silently broaden it.
  • Distinguish Bedrock's model API from AgentCore Gateway's inference routing. Compare routing products against the required controls, not the vendor name alone.
  • Check routing and authorisation separately from key management; a key/quota layer alone is not evidence that either is covered.
  • Do not rely on Gateway policy to control shell networking. It governs traffic through the Gateway only.

Treat the gateway's credentials as a separate trust boundary

Centralising model calls also concentrates high-value provider credentials and delegated identities. Prefer AWS role-based access and short-lived federation where supported; avoid exporting persistent provider keys to coding agents, CI runners, prompts or environment files. For keys that remain necessary, restrict access by workload, rotate and revoke on incident, monitor unusual usage and spend, and define an owner for response. An agent's ability to reach a gateway does not give it blanket authority to use every model or downstream credential. [25]

Threat example, not a gateway benchmark: Fireworks' November 2026 security bulletin reported exposure of some stored secrets and links to financially motivated LLMjacking. That incident is not evidence of a flaw in every LLM gateway; it shows why key custody, egress, quotas and rapid revocation belong in the architecture. Test stolen-token revocation, abnormal-spend alerts and gateway bypass paths before adoption. [26]

Gaps and open questions

  • AgentCore inference routing is documented, but the required region, API operations and control behaviour still need qualification for the selected configuration.[17]
  • Gateway failover must not silently broaden the approved-model policy. No automatic routing to unapproved models is acceptable as a fallback. Kiro's Auto routing is the cautionary example: current documentation says Auto can route to active models outside the administrator's approved list.[14][15]
  • Qualification needs the intended account and configuration: check denied models, fallback destinations, permission revocation, timeouts, costs and retained identity before adoption.

Next, record the team's approved-model list and the fallback behaviour it accepts — fail closed, or queue and retry — before adopting any gateway, then read the harness spoke for the managed harness this gateway sits beside.
